citations.assertion: Associated-family investigation only; James is not named in this packet. The original Pittsylvania bond of 1 February 1819 names Nathaniel Hendrick and William Glasgo as obligors for Nathaniel’s licence to marry Elizabeth Eudaly. Both names appear in the signature entries; William’s surname there is written Glasgow. The associated declaration, dated 30 January 1819 in Elizabeth Eudaly’s name, states that she has no objection to Nathaniel obtaining a marriage licence to marry her. William Glasgo is named under the witness heading. The matching endorsement reads Hendrick, marriage bond, to the Governor. These originals confirm the previously indexed William association and add the bride’s dated declaration. They name no parent or relationship between William, Elizabeth and James Glasgow-62. The 1819 bride is a specific possible continuation of the Elizabeth Glasgow who obtained a licence with Robert Eudaley in this county in December 1815: the given name, unusual married surname and continuing Glasgow associates fit. Neither packet calls her a widow or recites the earlier marriage, so that identity remains a candidate, not a proved remarriage or evidence of Robert’s death. A non-expert visual comparison of the 1819 and 1851 William signatures is compatible in broad cursive forms, but not diagnostic; the surety is not identified as the Little Fall Creek deponent or with any particular existing William profile. Existing William-3678 and William-563 remain weak unselected comparisons; their separate Wythe and Ohio accounts supply no specific Pittsylvania bridge. James’s father remains Unknown and unrated. No family attachment, vital field or confidence rating changes.
